I changed `src/solution.py` so an allocation is feasible exactly when the total requested amount of each resource is at most the amount available. I didn't run it or write any checks.

- **Removed the "leave something unallocated" rule.** The old code returned `False` when every resource was used up exactly. Now exact use is feasible, as the requirement says (`<=`).
- **Empty requests are now feasible.** Previously they were feasible only if some resource had positive capacity.
- **Removed the empty-`resources` error.** An empty `resources` dict used to raise `ValueError`. It no longer does.
- **Dropped two dead `None` checks.** They could never run, because the `isinstance` checks above them already reject `None`.

The function name, signature, input validation and summing logic are unchanged.
